limitations: Diagnostic runtime contexts are not clean timing measurements.
Active-dispatch ownership does not reveal allocation creation sites or erased source ancestry.
Event counts and CPU samples have different denominators and should not be compared as equivalent costs.
Fixed sampling periods can alias; raw and period-weighted results are both retained.
Private synchronous calls retain the active outer dispatch; known contexts can still hide inner functions.
Native FID binding is checked against every linked table pointer; lexical owners remain conditional on emitter provenance.
Raw ordered samples and sidecars remain in their original pinned captures; no duplicate event streams are written.
